beats.text: You wore the navy one. Bisola, her PA, checked you at the lift like a bouncer with an iPad. Madam Folake is seated. Your food is already ordered.
I chose for you. You'll like it. Sit, darling. Phone face down.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Her phone rings: 'Abuja Office'. She answers in a voice you haven't heard yet: soft, careful. 'Yes sir. Lagos. Alone.'

three_men.text: 'Dapo, pass the-- sorry. You. Pass the water.' She laughs a little too long.

widow.text: Her wedding ring catches the candlelight. When you look at it, she covers it with her other hand.

choices.label: Eat what she ordered. "Thank you, Madam."
choices.receipt: You ate what Madam ordered for you and took the envelope.

outcomes.text: She watches you eat like a project going well. At dessert Bisola hands you an envelope: 'Transport.' It is not transport money.

widow.text: She watches you eat and relaxes for the first time all night. The envelope comes anyway. 'Don't argue. I like giving.'

choices.label: Call the waiter back. Order for yourself.
choices.receipt: You ordered for yourself after Madam ordered for you.

outcomes.text: Bisola's pen stops. Madam studies you. 'Hm. You have opinions.' She hasn't decided if she likes them.

widow.text: She laughs, a real laugh. 'Good. My husband used to do that. Order me the same thing.'

three_men.text: 'Dapo always eats what I order.' Who is Dapo? She doesn't say. She sips her wine.

husband_alive.text: 'Don't make a scene.' She glances at the door. Then again.

choices.label: "Tonight, I'm paying." Card on the table.
choices.broke_text: Your card would decline in front of Bisola. Not today.
choices.receipt: You paid for your own date with Madam Folake.

outcomes.text: 'Put that away.' You don't. She stares at your card like an unfamiliar animal, then lets the waiter take it.

widow.text: She goes very quiet. 'Nobody has paid for me in five years.' She lets you. Her eyes are wet. She blames the pepper.

husband_alive.text: 'Put that away before anyone sees your name next to mine.' The waiter takes it anyway. She tips him to forget it.

three_men.text: 'Cute.' Bisola refunds you before you reach the lift: 'Madam doesn't allow that. From anyone.' Anyone.

choices.label: "Do you always order for people?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam why she orders for people.

outcomes.text: 'Always. It saves time. Time is the only thing I can't buy.' She looks at you properly for the first time.

widow.text: 'Since my husband died, I order for everyone. Somebody has to decide something.' She didn't mean to say that.

three_men.text: 'I order for all my--' She sips. 'For everyone I take out.'

husband_alive.text: 'I like to know what's coming.' Her phone buzzes on the table. She flinches.

choices.label: [Sugar] Order the lobster AND the wine list.
choices.receipt: You ordered the lobster and the wine list on Madam.

outcomes.text: 'Greedy. Good. Greed is honest.' Bisola adds you to a spreadsheet you will never see.

beats.text: Her Range Rover on the Link Bridge. Bisola up front with an iPad. On the seat beside you: a garment bag. Navy. Your size.
Change. The driver won't look. You're meeting my friends tonight and I can't have you in that.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Through the back glass: a grey Hilux, two cars behind. It takes every turn you take.

three_men.text: Bisola opens the boot for your old clothes. Inside: two more garment bags. Navy. Two other sizes.

widow.text: Bisola, without looking up: 'Madam takes calls from seven to nine. After nine, she is not available. To anyone.'

choices.label: Change into the navy. Smile.
choices.receipt: You let Madam dress you in the back of her car.

outcomes.text: It fits perfectly. That's the scary part. She fixes your collar: 'Now you look like mine.'

widow.text: It fits. She fixes your collar, then stops, hand on your chest. 'Sorry. Old habit.' She lets go slowly.

choices.label: "I dress myself, Madam."
choices.receipt: You refused to wear the outfit Madam chose.

outcomes.text: The car goes quiet. Bisola types something. Madam: 'Noted.' You go to the party in your own clothes, seated at the far end.

widow.text: She looks at you a long time, then laughs. 'Okay. Okay. Wear your thing. You look nice, actually.'

three_men.text: 'The others never argue.' Others. She says it like weather.

choices.label: "How do you know my size?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam how she knew your size.

outcomes.text: 'I know a lot of things.' She smiles. It doesn't reach anything.

widow.text: 'I used to buy my husband's clothes. I'm good with sizes.' She looks out at the lagoon for a long time.

three_men.text: 'Bisola has everybody's-- your size. On file.' On file.

husband_alive.text: 'I know. Other people know things too. That's why you'll wear what I say.' She checks the mirror.

choices.label: [Big Boy] Hand her a garment bag back: "Your turn."
choices.receipt: You brought Madam an outfit of your own choosing.

outcomes.text: Bisola gasps. Madam unzips it: a gele in your colours. She laughs for a full minute. 'Nobody has ever.'

beats.text: A 600-guest wedding in her VI hall. She walks you through it like a general. Every waiter straightens when she passes.
Stand next to me. Smile. Say nothing about yourself. People here talk.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Her clutch spills at the high table. A man's wedding ring rolls out. 'For luck,' she says, and zips the bag shut.

three_men.text: Bisola, into her headset: 'Yes, the new one is here. No, Saturday is their slot now. Tuesday stays Yaba.'

widow.text: A guest: 'Abuja misses you, Madam.' Her smile breaks for one second. 'I don't go to Abuja. Not anymore.'

choices.label: Smile. Say nothing. Be the accessory.
choices.receipt: You stood silently beside Madam all night.

outcomes.text: Four hours of smiling. Your cheeks hurt. She squeezes your hand under the table: 'Perfect.' Bisola sends ₦100k: 'Wages.'

choices.label: Introduce yourself properly. Full name, job, everything.
choices.receipt: You introduced yourself to Madam's guests.

outcomes.text: The aunties love you. Madam doesn't. 'I said nothing about yourself.' The drive home is very quiet.

widow.text: The aunties love you. Folake watches, then joins in: 'And funny, too.' She sounds proud. She sounds surprised to be proud.

husband_alive.text: An old man at table six writes your name on a napkin and pockets it. Madam sees. She goes pale.

choices.label: Pull her onto the dance floor.
choices.receipt: You pulled Madam onto the dance floor.

outcomes.text: The DJ switches to Fuji. Madam dances like she's 25 and owes nobody. The hall cheers.
'Not in public,' she hisses, and leaves the floor. You dance alone. The videographer gets everything.

three_men.text: The DJ switches to Fuji. Madam dances like she's 25 and owes nobody. The hall cheers.
The DJ stops the music and stares at you, then at her. Bisola mouths 'Dapo'. He plays a breakup song.

husband_alive.text: 'Not in public!' A man at the bar is filming. She covers her face with her fan and leaves.

choices.label: "Who are all these people to you?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam who everyone at the wedding was.

outcomes.text: 'Clients, enemies and family. At a wedding, same thing.' She gives you the whole map. You're on it now.

choices.label: [Runs] Work the room. Collect business cards.
choices.receipt: You networked at Madam's client's wedding.

outcomes.text: Forty cards. Three leads. Madam watches you hustle her own guests and can't decide whether to fire you or hire you.

beats.text: A calendar invite lands from Bisola. You never gave Bisola your email.
Madam: Tue 7–9pm. Dress code: white. Do not call before. Do not post. Accept by 5pm.
{tell}

three_men.text: Then a second text, clearly not for you: 'Confirming your Tuesday slot. Thursday is GRA.' Deleted.

husband_alive.text: A footnote at the bottom: 'No calls after 10pm. Madam speaks to Abuja at 10.'

widow.text: Then, separately: 'Madam doesn't take calls after 9. Please don't take it personally. She sleeps badly. - B.'

choices.label: Accept. White it is.
choices.receipt: You accepted Bisola's calendar invite without a word.

outcomes.text: Accepted. Bisola replies with a thumbs up and your measurements. You never sent your measurements.

choices.label: Decline. Propose Wednesday instead.
choices.receipt: You declined Madam's slot and proposed your own.

outcomes.text: Bisola: 'Madam doesn't do Wednesdays.' Then: 'Madam says Wednesday is fine.' Then: 'Don't do that again.'

widow.text: Bisola: 'Madam says yes.' Then a voice note from Folake herself, laughing: 'You argue with my PA? Brave. Wednesday.'

choices.label: Ask Bisola what Madam's other days are for.
choices.receipt: You asked Bisola what Madam's other evenings were for.

outcomes.text: Bisola: 'Board meetings.' Nobody has board meetings at 9pm. Bisola knows that you know that.

three_men.text: Bisola: 'Tuesday is Yaba. Thursday is GRA. You're Saturday. Don't tell Madam I said.' You didn't have to ask twice.

husband_alive.text: 'Madam's other days belong to Abuja.' Bisola never explains anything twice.

widow.text: 'Her other evenings are for the cemetery in Ikoyi and her accountant. Sorry. That was a lot.'

choices.label: Call Madam directly. Skip the PA.
choices.receipt: You called Madam directly instead of her PA.

outcomes.text: She picks on the first ring. 'Who gave you this number?' She did. 'Hm. Okay. Talk.'

husband_alive.text: She declines. Bisola texts: 'Never call Madam directly. People listen to her phone.' People?

widow.text: She picks up. Her voice cracks. 'Nobody calls me just to call me.' You talk for an hour.

choices.label: Call her at 10pm. See who answers.
choices.receipt: You called Madam at the hour she asked you never to.

outcomes.text: Straight to voicemail. Bisola texts at 10:01: 'Madam asked you not to.'

husband_alive.text: A man answers. Abuja accent. Calm. 'Who is this?' Then her voice in the background, and the line goes dead.

three_men.text: Dapo answers. 'She's in the shower. Who's this? Saturday?' He laughs. You don't.

widow.text: She answers, voice thick. 'At ten I listen to his old voicemails. Please. Not ten.'

choices.label: [Lover] Reply with a poem about white outfits.
choices.receipt: You replied to Madam's PA with a poem.

outcomes.text: Bisola forwards it to Madam. Madam replies with one word: 'Cute.' She saves it, though. You can tell.

beats.text: Third time this week: a grey Hilux behind your danfo at Ojuelegba. Same driver. Same toothpick. He doesn't even pretend.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: FCT plates. Abuja. The driver photographs you through his windscreen, then answers his phone: 'Yes sir. Same one.'

three_men.text: At the junction he leans out: 'Dapo! Madam said-- ah. Sorry. Wrong person. You people look alike.'

widow.text: Later Bisola texts: 'That's Madam's driver. She worries when you take danfo. I've told her it's too much.'

choices.label: Ignore it. Lagos is full of Hiluxes.
choices.receipt: You ignored the grey Hilux following you.

outcomes.text: You get home. The Hilux parks across the road, engine running. It's still there at midnight.

choices.label: Get off at the junction. Knock on his window.
choices.receipt: You knocked on the Hilux driver's window.

outcomes.text: He winds it down an inch. 'I'm just a driver.' He drives off.

husband_alive.text: 'Engineer says you should enjoy Lagos while you can.' He winds the window back up.
He photographs your face up close and drives off. Your hands shake for an hour.

three_men.text: 'I drive for Madam. I drive all of you. Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday.' All of you.

widow.text: 'Madam asked me to see you home. Her husband died on the road. She doesn't trust roads.'

choices.label: Photograph the plate. Quietly.
choices.receipt: You photographed the Hilux's plate.

outcomes.text: Plate saved. Future you will thank present you.

choices.label: Call Madam: "Is the grey Hilux yours?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam if the Hilux was hers.

outcomes.text: Silence. 'Which Hilux?' Then, too fast: 'Take a cab home. I'll send money.'

widow.text: 'Yes. I'm sorry. I'll call him off. I just need to know people get home.' She sounds ashamed of it.

husband_alive.text: 'It's not mine.' A long pause. 'Take a cab. Don't take danfo anymore. Please.'

choices.label: Text Bisola. Bisola has never lied to Madam.
choices.receipt: You asked Bisola whose Hilux it was.

outcomes.text: Bisola: 'I can't discuss vehicles.' Then: 'Be careful, though.'

husband_alive.text: Bisola: 'It's not Madam's. It's her husband's man. He's alive. In Abuja. Delete this.'

three_men.text: Bisola: 'Madam's driver. He checks on all three of you. Sorry. Two of you. I mean--'

widow.text: Bisola: 'Madam's driver. Since the accident she can't stand anyone she likes on the road. It's grief, not spying.'

choices.label: [Runs] Lose him through Balogun Market.
choices.receipt: You lost the Hilux in Balogun Market.

outcomes.text: Through the fabric section, out the back, onto a keke. He's lost. You're a legend. One of your shoes is still in Balogun.

beats.text: Her Ikoyi house. She slides a box across the marble: the newest phone, still sealed. Bisola has already set it up.
Your old phone embarrasses me. This one has everything you need. Mostly me.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Under the charger in the box: a man's wedding ring. 'For luck,' she says, and pockets it fast.

three_men.text: Bisola's handbag is open on the counter. Two more identical boxes inside.

widow.text: Pre-saved contacts: 'Madam', 'Bisola', 'Dr. Okoye'. Nobody in Abuja. 'I don't go to Abuja,' she says. You didn't ask.

choices.label: Take it. Use it. Say thank you.
choices.receipt: You took the phone Madam gave you and put yours away.

outcomes.text: She kisses your cheek. Your old phone goes into a drawer. Bisola has the drawer key.

widow.text: She sets it up with you, slowly. 'I just want to reach you. That's all it is.' It might be.

choices.label: "Thank you, but I'll keep my phone."
choices.receipt: You refused Madam's phone.

outcomes.text: She closes the box. 'Hm.' She doesn't argue. She also doesn't call you for a day.

widow.text: 'Fair. I'm too much sometimes.' She gives it to Bisola, whose phone screen has been cracked since 2022.

choices.label: "What else is installed on it?"
choices.receipt: You asked what was installed on Madam's phone.

outcomes.text: 'Nothing. Location sharing. Normal things.' Normal.

husband_alive.text: Settings: location shared with 'Madam', 'Bisola' and an Abuja number with no name.

three_men.text: Location shared with Madam. And a group chat already on it: 'Madam's Boys 🌹'. Three members.

widow.text: 'Location, so I know you're safe. Turn it off if you want.' You check. It turns off. She means it.

choices.label: [Runs] Take it. Keep your SIM in the old one.
choices.receipt: You took Madam's phone and kept your own SIM.

outcomes.text: Two phones. One for Madam, one for life. She never finds out. Probably.

beats.text: A furnished flat off Bourdillon Road. Two years' rent, paid. Bisola holds out the keys and a printed list of 'house rules'.
It's yours. Bisola keeps a spare key. No visitors after ten. That's all.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: The lease is signed 'A. Adeyemi, Abuja'. Not by her. She covers the signature with her thumb.

three_men.text: The doorman, carrying your box: 'Flat 2B? Ah. 2A is Madam's Yaba friend. Tuesdays.'

widow.text: Rule 4 on Bisola's list: 'Madam may call at 9pm only.' Rule 5: 'Madam is not to be left alone on Sundays.'

choices.label: Take the keys. Ikoyi is Ikoyi.
choices.receipt: You moved into the flat Madam pays for.

outcomes.text: You move in Friday. The view is criminal. Bisola visits 'to check the plumbing' twice a day.

widow.text: You move in. The rules sheet disappears on day two. 'Bisola overdoes it,' Folake says, embarrassed.

husband_alive.text: You move in. Night one, the grey Hilux parks outside. It already knew the address.

choices.label: "I'll pay my own rent, thank you."
choices.receipt: You turned down the flat and kept paying your own rent.

outcomes.text: Bisola looks at Madam like you've spoken Latin. Madam: 'Your pride is expensive. Keep it.' She sounds half impressed.

widow.text: 'Good.' She tears the rules sheet in half. 'I didn't want to buy you. I wanted you safe. Different thing.'

choices.label: "What happens to the flat if we end?"
choices.receipt: You asked what happens to the flat if it ends.

outcomes.text: 'Then it ends.' She smiles. 'Everything in Lagos has a notice period. Mine is one hour.'

widow.text: 'Then it's still yours. I'm not a landlord. I'm a woman who likes you.' Bisola writes that down.

husband_alive.text: 'Then you leave fast. Before anyone asks whose flat it was.' She isn't joking.

choices.label: Take it, but pay half the rent.
choices.broke_text: Half of Ikoyi rent is still Ikoyi rent.
choices.receipt: You paid half the rent on Madam's flat.

outcomes.text: She laughs at the alert. 'Half? You're a strange one.' She keeps it. That's respect, in her currency.

choices.label: Ask Bisola, privately: "Whose name is on the lease?"
choices.receipt: You asked Bisola whose name was on the lease.

outcomes.text: Bisola: 'Madam's company.' She hands you the keys anyway. 'Lock the door. Always.'

husband_alive.text: Bisola, whispering: 'Her husband's company. He pays. He'll know you're here before you unpack.'

three_men.text: Bisola: 'Madam's. Same as 2A and the one in GRA. She buys in bulk.'

widow.text: Bisola: 'Yours. She put it in your name yesterday. She'll pretend she didn't.'

choices.label: [Runs] Take it. Change the locks on day one.
choices.receipt: You changed the locks on Madam's flat.

outcomes.text: Bisola's key doesn't work on Monday. Madam calls: 'Clever.' It's the first time she sounds afraid of you.

beats.text: Breakfast at her Ikoyi house. Beside your plate: a contract. 'Brand Consultant, Folake Events. ₦500k monthly.' And an NDA. Twelve pages.
Sign, darling. It's just paperwork. It protects us both.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Clause 9: 'Consultant may be required to relocate on short notice.' Her phone buzzes: 'Abuja Office'. She lets it ring.

three_men.text: Page three, top line: 'Consultant: Dapo A--' crossed out, your name handwritten above.

widow.text: Bisola has initialled every page. 'I read everything before Madam signs. Since 2021.' Since 2021?

choices.label: Sign. ₦500k is ₦500k.
choices.receipt: You signed Madam's contract and NDA.

outcomes.text: Bisola stamps it. First salary lands in an hour. You've never been paid so well to never mention someone.

husband_alive.text: Paid. Clause 12, which you didn't read: 'Consultant consents to monitoring for security purposes.' Security from whom?

widow.text: It's a real job. On Monday she uses your ideas and credits you in front of her staff. Bisola nods at you like a colleague.

choices.label: "My lawyer reads it first."
choices.receipt: You asked for your lawyer to read the contract.

outcomes.text: 'Bring your lawyer.' She seems almost relieved that someone is careful.

husband_alive.text: Your lawyer calls back: 'Clauses 9, 12 and 14. Who is she hiding you from?'

three_men.text: Your lawyer: 'The document metadata has two previous consultants' names. Both men. Both under 30.'

choices.label: "₦800k, weekends free, my phone stays mine."
choices.receipt: You negotiated Madam's contract.

outcomes.text: She laughs. 'A negotiator.' She signs your version. You have weekends now.
'This is not a market.' She takes the contract back. Breakfast ends early.

choices.label: Tear it up: "I'm not your staff."
choices.receipt: You tore up Madam's contract.

outcomes.text: Bisola actually gasps. Madam watches the pieces fall. 'Then what are you?' You don't have an answer yet.

widow.text: Silence. Then: 'You're right. I'm sorry. I don't know how to do this without paperwork.'

choices.label: [Corporate] Redline it. Return it in an hour.
choices.receipt: You redlined Madam's contract.

outcomes.text: Track changes. Forty comments. She reads every one. 'Bisola, hire this one properly.'

husband_alive.text: Your redline deletes Clause 12. She deletes your redline. 'That clause isn't mine to remove.'

beats.text: Darling. Embarrassing. My accounts are frozen 'for review'. Six trucks are stuck at Ibafo on the expressway. ₦300k for diesel tonight. Monday, you'll have it back.
The richest person you know is asking you for money. At 11pm.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: 'Abuja froze-- the bank froze it.' She corrects herself in the very next message.

three_men.text: A second message: 'Thank you Tobi ❤️'. Deleted. 'Sorry. Autocorrect.'

widow.text: 'It's the estate case. In Abuja. I won't go there. Bisola is handling it.' She deletes two voice notes.

choices.label: Send ₦300k. She'd do it for you.
choices.broke_text: Your account said 'fuel? I'm the one on reserve.'
choices.receipt: You sent Madam ₦300k for diesel.

outcomes.text: Sent.

husband_alive.text: Monday: ₦600k back. 'Never tell anyone I asked.' She's scared, not broke.
Monday: nothing. Tuesday: 'My husband-- the bank is being difficult.' Husband. She said husband.

three_men.text: Monday: ₦300k back with a note: 'You passed.' Passed what? Bisola: 'She asked all three. You sent the most.'

widow.text: Monday, 8am: ₦500k back and a voice note, half crying: 'You trusted me. People only ever take from me.'

choices.label: Send ₦30k: "It's what I have."
choices.receipt: You sent Madam ₦30k.

outcomes.text: 'Every little helps,' she says. She has never said that sentence before in her life.

choices.label: Pay the filling station at Ibafo directly.
choices.receipt: You tried to pay the filling station directly.

outcomes.text: The station manager: 'Which trucks? No trucks here.' You keep your money.

widow.text: The manager confirms six of her trucks. You pay ₦50k direct; she covers the rest by morning. 'Smart,' she says.

husband_alive.text: 'Madam's trucks? Her husband's people took them back to Abuja last week.' Her husband.

three_men.text: 'Madam's trucks are fine. One young man already paid. Another one is paying now.'

choices.label: "Madam, I'm not your bank."
choices.receipt: You told Madam you're not her bank.

outcomes.text: 'Of course not. You're my sweetheart.' She doesn't call for a day. It feels like punishment. It is.

widow.text: 'Fair.' A long pause. 'Nobody says no to me. Thank you for that too.'

choices.label: "You said you never sleep till the trucks arrive."
choices.receipt: You remembered Madam never sleeps till her trucks arrive.

outcomes.text: 'I haven't slept. Two nights.' You stay on the phone till 3am. She doesn't mention the money again.

husband_alive.text: 'They're not my trucks anymore,' she whispers. 'Don't ask whose.'

beats.text: Owambe in Surulere. You're on Madam's arm in navy. A younger man walks in. Also navy. Same tailor. Same buttons.
Madam! You didn't tell me we were matching today. Who's this one?
{tell}

three_men.text: Dapo's navy is the same cut as yours. One size smaller. Bisola is suddenly very busy with her phone.

husband_alive.text: Through the hall's open doors: the grey Hilux, engine running. The driver is filming the high table.

widow.text: Dapo kisses her ring hand: 'Mummy, you still wear it?' She nods. Quietly. Mummy?

choices.label: Step to him: "Who are YOU?"
choices.receipt: You squared up to Dapo at the owambe.

outcomes.text: The music stops. Aunties lean in. Dapo laughs. Madam's face goes cold enough to store fish.

three_men.text: 'I'm Tuesday,' Dapo grins. 'You must be Saturday.' The aunty at table four chokes on her jollof.

widow.text: 'I'm her nephew, abeg calm down.' The hall laughs. Folake looks at you like you've disappointed her mother.

choices.label: Ask Madam quietly: "Who is he?"
choices.receipt: You quietly asked Madam who Dapo was.

outcomes.text: 'A family friend.' She fixes your collar instead of looking at you.

three_men.text: 'A friend from Yaba.' The way she says Yaba, it's an address and a timetable.

widow.text: 'My nephew. My late husband's brother's son. He thinks he's funny.' He is, a bit.

husband_alive.text: 'Nobody. Smile. People are watching.' Her eyes are on the door, not on Dapo.

choices.label: Out-dance him. In front of everyone.
choices.receipt: You had a dance-off with Dapo.

outcomes.text: The aunties pick a winner. It's you. Madam sprays you first, then Dapo, as consolation.
You pull something in your back mid-Shaku. Dapo helps you up. It's worse that he's nice.

choices.label: Leave her with him. Take a keke home.
choices.receipt: You left Madam at the owambe and went home.

outcomes.text: She calls nine times before you reach Ojuelegba. The tenth call is Bisola: 'Madam would like to know where you are.'

widow.text: She calls once: 'He's my nephew, you know. Come back. I'll make him dance with the aunties as punishment.'

choices.label: "Is he Tuesday's 'board meeting'?"
choices.receipt: You asked if Dapo was her Tuesday board meeting.

outcomes.text: She stares at you. 'You listen too well.' She doesn't answer.

three_men.text: Madam doesn't answer. Dapo does: 'Tuesdays, yes. Who told you?'

widow.text: She laughs, shocked. 'Tuesday IS my board meeting! He sits on the board.' He does. Badly.

choices.label: "Nice navy. Same tailor? Same sponsor?"
choices.receipt: You asked Dapo if you shared a tailor and a sponsor.

outcomes.text: Dapo laughs. 'Same everything, my friend.' Madam pinches the bridge of her nose.

three_men.text: 'Same sponsor,' Dapo says, and toasts you. Madam closes her eyes. Bisola starts typing.

widow.text: 'Same aunty,' Dapo says. 'She dressed me for my wedding too. She dresses everyone she loves.'

choices.label: [Big Boy] Spray Dapo. Bigger notes. Make it clear.
choices.receipt: You outsprayed Dapo at the owambe.

outcomes.text: The hall roars. Dapo bows, collects every note and leaves. A professional.

beats.text: Her VIP lounge in VI, full of her clients. Madam looks at your shoes. Then at the room.
Darling. Those shoes. Go and change. Bisola has a pair in the car. Now, please.
Size already confirmed, Madam.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Her phone buzzes on the table: 'Abuja Office'. She goes pale and pushes it under a napkin.

three_men.text: Bisola, to the waiter: 'Same order as last Thursday's guest. And Tuesday's.'

widow.text: She twists her wedding ring while she says it. Round and round. Like she's somewhere else.

choices.label: Change the shoes. Smile at the clients.
choices.receipt: You changed your shoes because Madam told you to.

outcomes.text: The new shoes are better. That's the worst part. She squeezes your hand: 'Thank you.' The room approves.

choices.label: "I dress myself, Madam." Loudly.
choices.receipt: You told Madam off in front of her clients.

outcomes.text: The lounge goes quiet. Somebody laughs. Madam doesn't. 'Bisola, the bill.' The night is over.

widow.text: She blinks. Then, to the room: 'This one has opinions. I like opinions.' Later, alone: 'Sorry. I panic in rooms.'

choices.label: Keep your shoes. Talk to her later, alone.
choices.receipt: You kept your shoes and spoke to Madam privately.

outcomes.text: In the car: 'Don't correct me in front of people. Correct me here.' She listens. Not long. But she listens.

widow.text: In the car she says: 'My husband wore shoes like that. It hurt to look at.' Oh.

choices.label: Wear Bisola's shoes. Carry yours in your hand.
choices.receipt: You wore her shoes and carried your own.

outcomes.text: The clients find it hilarious. Madam pretends not to. She fails.

choices.label: "Let's leave. Amala in Surulere. Shoes optional."
choices.receipt: You took Madam out for amala in Surulere.

outcomes.text: She stares. Then she kicks off her heels under the table. 'Bisola, cancel everything.' Best night in years, she says.

choices.label: [Big Boy] Buy every client in the lounge new shoes.
choices.receipt: You bought shoes for Madam's entire lounge.

outcomes.text: Twelve clients. Twelve pairs. Madam is speechless for the first time in recorded history.

beats.text: The Parlour, 9am: you stepping out of her Range Rover. Caption: 'Madam Folake's new pet 🐶 Kept in Ikoyi.' 3,000 likes.
Your group chat: 'Kept and content 😂'. Your cousin: 'Ask if she has a sister.'
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Second photo in the post: you at a bus stop, shot from inside a grey Hilux. Who took that one?

three_men.text: Top comment, from @dapo_spins: 'Welcome to the team 🤝'. 400 likes.

widow.text: Bisola texts at 9:04: 'Madam has seen it. She's asking if you're okay. She is not asking anything else.'

choices.label: Repost it: "Kept? I'm employed. Different thing."
choices.receipt: You flexed on the Parlour about being kept.

outcomes.text: The Parlour loves it. You go from punchline to icon in an hour.
Madam sees it. 'You think this is funny?' It was. Until now.

choices.label: Comment: "Fake. That's my aunty."
choices.receipt: You told the Parlour Madam was your aunty.

outcomes.text: She sees it. 'Your aunty.' She doesn't speak to you until evening, and then only about logistics.

choices.label: Send it to Madam: "Can you handle this?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam to make the post disappear.

outcomes.text: It's gone in twenty minutes. The blog posts an apology. Nobody knows how. Everybody suspects.

husband_alive.text: 'I can't. Not this one. Stay indoors today.' She's frightened. Of a blog?

widow.text: Gone in ten minutes. Then she calls: 'Are you okay? I'm sorry my life lands on you.'

choices.label: Say nothing. Go to work. Let it die.
choices.receipt: You ignored the Parlour post.

outcomes.text: It dies by Thursday. Your coworkers call you 'Ikoyi' for the rest of your career.

choices.label: Comment: "Kept AND content. Next question."
choices.receipt: You owned being kept on the Parlour.

outcomes.text: The Parlour can't roast someone who agrees. Madam screenshots it and sends it to Bisola with three crowns.

husband_alive.text: The Parlour loves it. So does a grey Hilux account that follows you within the hour.

choices.label: Call her and ask how SHE feels about it.
choices.receipt: You asked Madam how she felt about the post.

outcomes.text: She's quiet. 'Nobody asks me that.' Then: 'Embarrassed. For you. Not of you.'

beats.text: 6am. A man in a grey kaftan at your gate. Polite. Patient. He has clearly been here before.
I work for Engineer Adeyemi. Madam's husband, in Abuja. He'd like this to stop. This envelope is ₦1m. The other one has photographs.
{tell}

husband_alive.text: Behind him at your gate: the grey Hilux. FCT plates. Engine running, like always.

choices.label: Take the ₦1m. Leave Lagos for a while.
choices.receipt: You took the husband's ₦1m to disappear.

outcomes.text: You take the money and the next bus to Ibadan. Madam calls forty times. You let it ring. You're paid and you're alive.

choices.label: Call Madam on speaker. In front of him.
choices.receipt: You called Madam on speaker in front of her husband's man.

outcomes.text: She picks up crying before you speak. 'I'm sorry. I thought he wouldn't bother with you. Go inside. Lock the door.'

choices.label: "Tell the Engineer I'm not scared."
choices.receipt: You told her husband's man you weren't scared.

outcomes.text: Mr. Sule nods, almost respectful. 'I'll tell him.' That night your landlord gives you notice. No reason given.
'You should be,' he says, gently. The Hilux follows you to work. And home. And to church.

choices.label: Photograph him. Post it on the Parlour.
choices.receipt: You posted her husband's man on the Parlour.

outcomes.text: The Parlour explodes: 'Madam Folake's HUSBAND is alive?!' By noon, her bookings are cancelling. By night, so are you.

choices.label: Hand back the envelopes. Close the gate. Block her.
choices.receipt: You returned the envelopes and walked away from Madam.

outcomes.text: You hand both envelopes back unopened, lock the gate and block her number. The Hilux leaves. It doesn't come back.

choices.label: "Your plate's been in my phone since day two."
choices.receipt: You showed Mr. Sule the plate photo you'd taken.

outcomes.text: He reads his own plate off your screen and stops smiling. 'Nobody needs police.' He leaves. The Hilux doesn't come back.

choices.label: "She said the Hilux wasn't hers. Now I know whose."
choices.receipt: You told Mr. Sule you'd worked out whose Hilux it was.

outcomes.text: Mr. Sule: 'She told you the truth, then. That's new.' He almost sounds sorry for both of you.

choices.label: "So he's the ten o'clock call."
choices.receipt: You worked out who calls Madam at 10pm.

outcomes.text: Mr. Sule's eyebrows lift. 'Every night at ten, he checks on her. Now he checks on you.'

choices.label: "Clause 12. 'Monitoring for security.' That was him."
choices.receipt: You connected the NDA's monitoring clause to her husband.

outcomes.text: He smiles for the first time. 'You read your contract. Most don't.' He tears up the photographs in front of you.

choices.label: "Tell the Engineer to refund my diesel money."
choices.receipt: You asked her husband's man to refund your money.

outcomes.text: Mr. Sule makes one call. The alert lands before he reaches the Hilux. 'The Engineer pays his wife's debts. Then he collects.'
'The Engineer doesn't pay for his wife's friends.' He leaves. So does your money, forever.

beats.text: Her birthday dinner on the Ikoyi rooftop. Bisola made one mistake: she seated all three of you at the same table.
Name cards: 'Tuesday'. 'Thursday'. 'Saturday'. You're Saturday.
Bisola. My office. Tomorrow. Everyone else: happy birthday to me.
{tell}

three_men.text: She looks down the table: 'Dapo, Tobi, darling--' It's the first time she's gotten all three right.

choices.label: Raise a glass: "To the schedule!"
choices.receipt: You toasted Madam's schedule in front of the whole rooftop.

outcomes.text: Dapo laughs first, then Tobi. The whole terrace toasts the schedule. Madam doesn't laugh. Then, finally, she does.

choices.label: Team up with Dapo and Tobi. Invoice her together.
choices.receipt: You invoiced Madam together with her other two men.

outcomes.text: Three invoices, one total: 'emotional logistics'. She pays your share, ₦1m, with a smile that will haunt you.

choices.label: Ask her quietly which of you she actually loves.
choices.receipt: You asked Madam which of you she loved.

outcomes.text: She looks at the three of you for a long time. 'Saturday.' Dapo and Tobi leave together, comparing receipts.
'All of you. Differently.' She means it. That's worse.

choices.label: Leave your name card on the cake. Walk.
choices.receipt: You left your name card and walked out of her birthday.

outcomes.text: You leave 'Saturday' face up beside the candles. Your Saturdays are yours again.

choices.label: "Tuesday. Dapo. We've met. Nice tailor."
choices.receipt: You greeted Dapo like an old colleague.

outcomes.text: Dapo high-fives you. Tobi asks for your tailor's number. Madam realises she has lost control of her own birthday.

choices.label: "Board meetings. Tuesdays and Thursdays. Happy birthday."
choices.receipt: You told Madam you'd known about her 'board meetings'.

outcomes.text: Madam puts down her fork. 'You knew.' 'Since day two.' She looks at you differently now. Like an equal.

choices.label: "Bisola told me. Tuesday's Yaba, Thursday's GRA."
choices.receipt: You revealed that Bisola had told you the schedule.

outcomes.text: Bisola stands up, sits down, stands up again. Madam doesn't even look at her. She looks at you.

beats.text: Midnight, her Ikoyi house. Bisola leaves a funeral programme on the table: 'Adewale, 1971–2021'. Then she leaves the room.
He died on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. In one of our trucks. I control everything now because I couldn't control that.
{tell}

widow.text: She takes off the ring for the first time since you met her, and holds it out to you in her palm.

choices.label: Sit with her. Listen till she's done.
choices.receipt: You sat with Madam and listened.

outcomes.text: She talks till 3am: the trucks, the funeral, the five years. Then she falls asleep on your shoulder, ring in her hand.

choices.label: "I'm here. But my phone and my Saturdays stay mine."
choices.receipt: You stayed, and kept your phone and your Saturdays.

outcomes.text: She laughs and cries at the same time. 'Deal. Bisola will hate it.' Bisola, from the corridor: 'I do.'

choices.label: Post the programme: "Grief or control? Discuss."
choices.receipt: You posted her late husband's funeral programme on the Parlour.

outcomes.text: The Parlour argues for a week. Folake reads every comment. She never calls again.

choices.label: "This is too heavy for me." Leave gently.
choices.receipt: You left Madam gently.

outcomes.text: You kiss her forehead and go. Bisola sees you out. 'Thank you for being gentle,' she says.

choices.label: "That's why you don't sleep till the trucks arrive."
choices.receipt: You remembered why she waits up for her trucks.

outcomes.text: She stares. 'You remembered that.' Then she cries properly, for the first time in five years.

choices.label: "How was your day? Really."
choices.receipt: You asked Madam how her day really was.

outcomes.text: 'Terrible,' she says, and laughs. 'Thank you for asking. Nobody asks. They invoice.'

choices.label: "Was navy his colour?"
choices.receipt: You asked if navy had been her husband's colour.

outcomes.text: 'Every Sunday for twenty years.' She touches your sleeve. 'I'll stop dressing you. I promise.'

beats.text: Bisola arrives at your office with an envelope: your exact bill, refunded, and a note in Madam's handwriting.
Nobody pays for me. I didn't sleep. Explain yourself. Thursday. My house. I'm cooking.

choices.label: Keep the refund. Go on Thursday.
choices.receipt: You kept the refund and went to Madam's for dinner.

outcomes.text: She cooks ewa agoyin herself, badly, and laughs at it with you. Bisola eats the leftovers in the car.

three_men.text: She cooks. Halfway through, Bisola whispers: 'She has never cooked for the others.' The others.

choices.label: Return the envelope: "It was a gift."
choices.receipt: You returned Madam's refund.

outcomes.text: Bisola brings it back. You return it. Bisola brings it back. On round four Madam calls: 'Fine. Stubborn. Thursday.'

widow.text: On round four, Folake calls herself, laughing: 'Fine. You win. My husband was stubborn too.'

husband_alive.text: On round three Bisola whispers: 'Please take it. Madam says no receipts with your name on them. People check.'

choices.label: "I'll bring dessert. From Surulere."
choices.receipt: You brought Madam puff-puff from Surulere.

outcomes.text: You bring puff-puff in a nylon bag. She eats eleven. 'Don't tell Bisola.'

beats.text: A garment bag at your door. Navy. Again. A note is pinned to it:
Madam insists. Kindly wear it tonight. She has asked me to say please. Please.

choices.label: Wear it. Pick your battles.
choices.receipt: You wore the navy outfit Madam sent.

outcomes.text: She sees you and exhales. 'Thank you.' You look great. You hate that you look great.

husband_alive.text: 'Navy is invisible,' she says, seating you at the back of her table. Invisible to whom?

choices.label: Return it with a note: "I dress myself."
choices.receipt: You sent the navy outfit back.

outcomes.text: Bisola sends a voice note: a long, tired sigh. Then: 'Madam says okay. Madam says... okay.'

widow.text: Folake calls: 'You're right. I'll stop. It was his colour. I'm sorry.'

choices.label: Send back a gele in your colours, for her.
choices.receipt: You sent Madam a gele you chose.

outcomes.text: She wears it to an owambe. The aunties ask who chose it. She says your name, loudly.

beats.text: 3am. The phone she gave you lights up on its own: 'Location shared with 3 people.' You only know two of them.

choices.label: Open the settings. See who's watching.
choices.receipt: You checked who was tracking the phone Madam gave you.

outcomes.text: Madam. Bisola. And 'Device 3', refreshing your location every minute.

husband_alive.text: Madam. Bisola. And an Abuja number with no name, refreshing every minute.

three_men.text: Madam. Bisola. And 'Madam's iPad (GRA)'. The iPad is at an address in Ikeja GRA.

widow.text: Madam, Bisola, and 'Dr. Okoye'. Her doctor. In case you collapse. She worries in very strange ways.

choices.label: Turn sharing off. Go back to sleep.
choices.receipt: You turned off location sharing.

outcomes.text: At 6am Bisola calls: 'Madam noticed. She'd like to know why.'

choices.label: Put her phone in a drawer. Use your old one.
choices.receipt: You put Madam's phone away and used your own.

outcomes.text: Your old phone feels light. Free. It has 34 unread messages from your actual friends.

choices.label: Text Madam: "Who is the third person?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam who the third tracker was.

outcomes.text: She replies at 3:01am. Awake. 'Security. Go back to sleep, darling.'

widow.text: 'My doctor. In case you fall. I lost someone on a road once.' You turn it off together, on the phone.

beats.text: A DM from an account with no picture, replying to your 'Kept? I'm employed' post.
Funny post. Enjoy Ikoyi while it lasts.

choices.label: "Who is this?"
choices.receipt: You asked the stranger who they were.

outcomes.text: Read. Then the account disappears.

husband_alive.text: 'Ask her husband how long things last.' Then a photo of your gate, taken this morning.

three_men.text: 'It lasted a year for me. Then she found a Saturday. - D.'

widow.text: 'Her late husband's sister. I post nonsense. Ignore me.' Then: 'Actually, look after her.'

choices.label: Forward it to Madam.
choices.receipt: You forwarded the DM to Madam.

outcomes.text: 'Delete your post, darling. Please.' It's the 'please' that scares you.

husband_alive.text: 'Delete it. Now. And stay home tonight.' She's whispering.

widow.text: 'That's my sister-in-law. She hates everyone I like. So she likes you a bit.'

choices.label: Delete the post. Block. Breathe.
choices.receipt: You deleted your post and blocked the stranger.

outcomes.text: Deleted. The screenshots are not.

beats.text: Your week, from Madam: every evening booked. Your sister's birthday on Saturday has been declined on your behalf. Gift sent.
You never told Bisola you have a sister. Madam is watching you read it.

choices.label: Go along. Your sister will understand.
choices.receipt: You let Madam cancel your sister's birthday for you.

outcomes.text: Your sister sends a voice note: 'So we don't see you again?' You listen to it twice, locked in Madam's bathroom.

choices.label: "I'm going to my sister's. Cancel me."
choices.receipt: You told Madam you were going to your sister's birthday.

outcomes.text: Bisola: 'Madam has... noted.' Saturday you dance with your sister till 2am. Madam doesn't call. That is its own message.

choices.label: Call your Bestie. Read the message out loud.
choices.receipt: You read Madam's schedule to your Bestie.

outcomes.text: Bestie: 'How does she know you have a sister? HOW?' You don't have an answer. You go to the party.

choices.label: Block them both. Go to your sister's. Stay there.
choices.receipt: You blocked Madam and her PA and went to your sister's.

outcomes.text: You sleep on your sister's couch for a week. She asks no questions. She makes you eba every night.

choices.label: "What are you scared of if I'm out of sight?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam what she was afraid of.

outcomes.text: Silence. Then Madam, not Bisola: 'Everything.' It's the most honest thing she's said. It doesn't make the schedule okay.

beats.text: Your old phone. Give it to me. You don't need it. You have mine.
Her hand is out. Bisola holds a small bag, open, ready. Nobody is smiling.

choices.label: Hand it over. You don't need it.
choices.receipt: You handed Madam your own phone.

outcomes.text: Bisola drops it in the bag. Your contacts, your photos, your mother's voice notes. Gone in one zip.

choices.label: "No. My phone is mine."
choices.receipt: You refused to give Madam your phone.

outcomes.text: Her hand stays out for a long time. Then it drops. 'Bisola, leave us.' You keep your phone. The room stays cold.

choices.label: "Let me back it up first." Call your Bestie.
choices.receipt: You called your Bestie when Madam asked for your phone.

outcomes.text: From the toilet. Bestie: 'Back it up? Babe, LEAVE.' You don't hand it over. You go home.

choices.label: Pocket your phone. Walk out.
choices.receipt: You walked out of Madam's house with your phone.

outcomes.text: Past Bisola, past the gate, onto Bourdillon Road. The phone in your pocket rings. It's your mum. You pick up.

choices.label: "You gave me your phone so you could take mine."
choices.receipt: You named what the gift phone was for.

outcomes.text: She doesn't deny it. 'I need to know where you are.' 'You already do,' you say. 'That's the problem.'

beats.text: 6pm, outside your office in Yaba. Her driver is at the gate. Engine on. Back door open.
Madam says I should carry you. Straight home. Only home. She'll call you there at seven to check.

choices.label: Get in. It's easier.
choices.receipt: You let Madam's driver take you straight home.

outcomes.text: The car smells of her perfume. At 7:00 exactly, the landline in the flat rings. You didn't know there was a landline.

choices.label: "Tell Madam I'll take the BRT." Walk.
choices.receipt: You refused Madam's driver and took the BRT.

outcomes.text: He follows you to the BRT stop at walking pace. Then he drives off. You ride home with strangers. It feels like air.

choices.label: Leave with your colleagues. Loudly. As a group.
choices.receipt: You left work in a group to avoid Madam's driver.

outcomes.text: Six of you, one danfo, one confused driver crawling behind. A colleague asks, 'Is that your security?' You laugh. You shouldn't have to.

choices.label: Drop her phone in his window. "We're done."
choices.receipt: You returned Madam's phone through the driver and left.

outcomes.text: 'Give it to Madam.' You walk to Ojuelegba. Nobody follows. You check three times. Nobody follows.

choices.label: Photograph his plate. Tell him you did.
choices.receipt: You photographed Madam's driver's plate.

outcomes.text: He sees the camera. 'Madam won't like that.' 'Madam can call me,' you say, and walk.

beats.text: You come home to the Ikoyi flat. Your key doesn't turn. New lock. A note on the door in Bisola's handwriting:
Madam has your new key. She'd like you to collect it in person. Tonight. Alone.

choices.label: Go to her house. Collect the key.
choices.receipt: You went to Madam's house to collect your new key.

outcomes.text: She hands it over slowly, holding your fingers. 'Now you know whose door it is.' You nod. You don't sleep.

choices.label: Call a locksmith. Pack your things tonight.
choices.receipt: You called a locksmith and packed your things.

outcomes.text: The locksmith reads the lease: not in your name. He opens the door anyway, for ₦10k and pity. You pack before midnight.

choices.label: Sleep at your sister's. Call your Bestie on the way.
choices.receipt: You slept at your sister's instead.

outcomes.text: Bestie: 'She changed the LOCK?' Your sister opens the door without a word and hands you a wrapper.

choices.label: Leave the old key under the mat. Never come back.
choices.receipt: You left the key under the mat and never went back.

outcomes.text: Everything you own in there is replaceable. You check. It is.

beats.text: Those Ikoyi restaurants bore me, you know. Underneath this gele, I'm a Bodija amala woman. Ewedu, gbegiri, the works. Don't tell my clients.

choices.label: "Amala, ewedu, gbegiri. Your secret is safe."
choices.receipt: You caught that Madam is an amala woman at heart.

outcomes.text: 'I knew you'd understand. You have amala energy.' Highest compliment she has.

choices.label: "Bodija? I thought you were Ikoyi-born."
choices.receipt: You assumed Madam was Ikoyi-born.

outcomes.text: 'Nobody is Ikoyi-born, darling. We all arrived.'

choices.label: "Send me something to wear for next time?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam to send you an outfit.

outcomes.text: Bisola sends ₦50k 'for outfit' and your measurements. You still never sent your measurements.

beats.text: Goodnight, darling. One rule: never call me at 10pm. Not 9:59, not 10:01. Ten o'clock is my quiet hour. Sleep well.

choices.label: "Ten is your quiet hour. I won't call."
choices.receipt: You noted Madam's 10pm rule.

outcomes.text: 'Thank you.' The relief in her voice is too big for a rule about phone calls.

choices.label: "Quiet hour for what?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam what happens at 10pm.

outcomes.text: 'For me.' A long pause. 'Goodnight.'

choices.label: "Can I call at 9:30 then? 😏"
choices.receipt: You tried to negotiate a 9:30 call.

outcomes.text: 'You can call Bisola at 9:30.'

beats.text: Busy week. Tuesdays and Thursdays I have board meetings till late. Don't wait up. Saturday is ours 😊

choices.label: "Tuesday, Thursday: board. Saturday: us. Noted."
choices.receipt: You noted Madam's Tuesday and Thursday 'board meetings'.

outcomes.text: 'Exactly. You understand schedules. I like that in a person.'

choices.label: "Which boards meet at 9pm?"
choices.receipt: You asked which boards meet at 9pm.

outcomes.text: 'Important ones.' Then a single 😊. It doesn't help.

choices.label: "Saturday! What should I wear?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam what to wear on Saturday.

outcomes.text: 'Bisola will send it.' Of course she will.

beats.text: Can't sleep. My trucks are on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway tonight. I never sleep till all of them arrive. Old habit. Talk to me till they do?

choices.label: "I'll stay up till the last truck reaches Ibadan."
choices.receipt: You stayed up with Madam until her trucks arrived.

outcomes.text: You talk till 3am. At 3:04 she says 'All in.' Then she falls asleep mid-sentence.

choices.label: "Don't you trust your drivers?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam why she doesn't trust her drivers.

outcomes.text: 'I trust drivers. I don't trust roads.' She ends the call.

choices.label: "Send me data so I can stay on the call 😅"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam for data money.

outcomes.text: ₦5k for data. 'You're funny. Stay on the line.'

beats.text: Seven meetings, two weddings, one fight with a caterer about small chops. Nobody ever asks me how my day was. They just ask for things. Anyway. How was yours?

choices.label: "Forget mine. How was YOUR day, really?"
choices.receipt: You asked Madam about her day and meant it.

outcomes.text: She talks for twenty minutes. At the end: 'Thank you. That was nice.' She sounds surprised.

choices.label: "Mine was long too! Let me tell you..."
choices.receipt: You told Madam about your day instead.

outcomes.text: She listens. She's good at it. She doesn't get a turn.

choices.label: "Small chops fight? Who won?"
choices.receipt: You asked who won the small chops fight.

outcomes.text: 'Me. I always win. That's the problem.'

beats.text: Bisola will call you about Saturday. Bisola has never lied to me in nine years. If Bisola says it, believe it. If I say it, check with Bisola 😂

choices.label: "Bisola: the source of truth. Got it."
choices.receipt: You noted that Bisola never lies.

outcomes.text: 'Exactly.' She doesn't realise what she just gave you.

choices.label: "Why would I need to check you?"
choices.receipt: You asked why you'd need to check Madam's word.

outcomes.text: 'Joke, darling. Mostly.'

choices.label: "Can Bisola send me transport?"
choices.receipt: You asked Bisola for transport money.

outcomes.text: ₦10k in thirty seconds, plus a template for 'future transport requests'.
